title: Acknowledge hospital HMI fault and retry tote operation
summary: Source-specific incident recovery for a hospital-area HMI fault at UPS Haslet TX (TXRTH). The incident evidence supports opening the hospital HMI where the fault is shown, not unplugging the HMI, using the acknowledge control, retrying the operation, confirming the tote at the hospital is tote ID 28, and verifying the area is back to normal.
when_to_use: Use when the hospital-area HMI is showing a fault and the source-supported recovery path is to acknowledge the fault on the HMI, retry the operation, confirm the tote identity at the hospital area, and verify the issue is cleared.
not_for: Do not use this procedure as guidance to unplug the HMI.
Do not use this procedure for faults that do not clear after acknowledge and retry, because the incident does not provide additional safe recovery steps.
Do not use this procedure to perform undocumented HMI changes, configuration changes, or other unsupported recovery actions.

responsibilities: Access the hospital-area HMI showing the fault.
Use the on-screen acknowledge control instead of unplugging the HMI.
Retry the operation from the HMI or associated tote flow as supported by the incident.
Confirm whether the tote at the hospital is tote ID 28.
Verify and report whether the area is 'all good' after retry.

safety_notes: Do not unplug the HMI when this fault is shown; the incident explicitly advised against unplugging it.
Do not perform undocumented changes beyond acknowledge, retry, tote ID confirmation, and status verification supported by the incident evidence.
access_or_tools_needed: Ability to view the tote ID at the hospital area
Support communication channel if the retry does not clear the fault

access_required: Ability to observe the tote at the hospital area
system_preconditions: A fault is currently shown on the hospital-area HMI.

steps.title: Open the hospital-area HMI showing the fault
steps.purpose: Locate the exact HMI and fault condition referenced in the incident before taking action.
steps.instruction: Go to the hospital area and open or view the HMI that is currently showing the fault condition.
steps.expected_result: The operator is viewing the hospital-area HMI where the fault is displayed.
steps.healthy_condition: The correct hospital-area HMI is identified and the fault condition is visible for review.
steps.failure_condition: The operator cannot locate the hospital-area HMI or cannot confirm that the displayed issue matches the reported fault.

actions.label: View hospital HMI fault
actions.exact_action: Open the HMI at the hospital area where the fault is being shown.

stop_or_escalate_if: The HMI cannot be accessed or the reported fault cannot be confirmed on the hospital-area screen.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The HMI at the hospital is showing a fault. Should I unplug it?

steps.title: Do not unplug the HMI; use acknowledge
steps.purpose: Prevent an unsupported action and use the source-backed recovery control instead.
steps.instruction: Do not unplug the HMI. Use the on-screen acknowledge control for the displayed fault.
steps.expected_result: The operator avoids unplugging the HMI and selects the acknowledge option on the fault screen.
steps.healthy_condition: The HMI remains connected and the acknowledge action is available and used.
steps.failure_condition: The acknowledge option is not available, or the operator is considering an unsupported action such as unplugging the HMI.

actions.label: Acknowledge HMI fault
actions.exact_action: Do not unplug the HMI when the fault is shown; use the on-screen acknowledge control instead.

stop_or_escalate_if: The HMI does not present an acknowledge option.
The only apparent next action would be unplugging the HMI.
The operator cannot safely proceed using the on-screen acknowledge control.

steps.title: Acknowledge the fault and retry the operation
steps.purpose: Apply the incident-supported recovery action to clear the fault and resume the tote operation.
steps.instruction: Hit acknowledge on the HMI and try the operation again from the HMI or associated tote flow.
steps.expected_result: The fault is cleared or the operation is retried successfully after acknowledge.
steps.healthy_condition: The HMI accepts acknowledge and the operation can be retried without the same fault immediately blocking progress.
steps.failure_condition: The fault remains active, immediately returns, or the operation cannot be retried successfully.
stop_or_escalate_if: The fault does not clear after acknowledge and retry.
The same fault immediately returns after retry.
The operation cannot be retried from the HMI or associated tote flow.

steps.title: Confirm the tote ID at the hospital area
steps.purpose: Validate the specific tote identity referenced during incident recovery.
steps.instruction: Check the tote at the hospital area and confirm whether it is tote ID 28.
steps.expected_result: The tote at the hospital area is positively identified.
steps.healthy_condition: The tote at the hospital is confirmed as tote ID 28, matching the incident validation.
steps.failure_condition: The tote ID cannot be read, cannot be confirmed, or does not match the expected tote ID 28.

actions.label: Verify tote ID
actions.exact_action: Check whether the tote at the hospital is tote ID 28.

stop_or_escalate_if: The tote ID cannot be confirmed.
The tote at the hospital is not tote ID 28.
The tote identity is ambiguous after retry.

steps.title: Confirm recovery status is all good
steps.purpose: Verify the incident-supported end condition before closing the recovery action.
steps.instruction: Confirm that the issue is cleared and the hospital area is back to normal before ending the procedure.
steps.expected_result: The operator confirms the area is 'all good' after the retry.
steps.healthy_condition: The tote at hospital is confirmed as 28 and the operator reports the area is all good.
steps.failure_condition: The operator cannot confirm normal status or any fault symptoms remain after retry.

actions.label: Verify normal status
actions.exact_action: Confirm the system is 'all good' after the retry before ending the procedure.

stop_or_escalate_if: The operator cannot confirm the area is all good.

Normal tote operation is not restored.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Yes the tote at hospital is 28 Yes Sir all good

success_criteria: The hospital-area HMI fault is acknowledged without unplugging the HMI.
The operation can be retried after acknowledge.
The tote at the hospital area is confirmed as tote ID 28.
The operator confirms the area is 'all good' after retry.
healthy_conditions: Hospital-area HMI fault is no longer blocking the operation after acknowledge and retry.
The tote at the hospital is identified as ID 28.
The operator reports normal status: 'all good'.
failure_conditions: The fault does not clear after acknowledge and retry.
The HMI cannot be safely recovered using the on-screen acknowledge control.
The tote ID at the hospital cannot be confirmed as part of validation.
The operator cannot confirm the area is back to normal.
escalation_guidance: If the fault does not clear after acknowledge and retry, stop and escalate; the incident does not provide further safe recovery steps.
Escalate if the acknowledge option is unavailable or the HMI cannot be used without unplugging it.
Escalate if tote ID validation at the hospital area cannot be completed.
